reason: The observation is accurate and the fix and the class are both wrong, which is what decides it. Driven in chromium at 1440x960 and at 390x844 with touch, ?v=light, states full/quiet/first-run/loading, I enumerated every visible text node inside .card.ages: at 1440 it is exactly "How long open work has been sitting", "OLDEST · 41 DAYS", "A FORTNIGHT", and the ticks today/15d/30d/45d, over six hollow and three solid discs; at 390 the same seven strings in a 342x263 card. So the seat is right that no rest-state string names a job and none names the interaction, and right that the .sr paragraph and the nine aria-labels leave the AX tree richer than the screen. Three things then break it. (1) THE FIX IS IN THE WRONG VOICE AND WOULD MAKE THE CARD WORSE. .t-label is lately.html:150 — 11px Geist Mono, letter-spacing var(--track-label), text-transform: uppercase. The proposed paragraph renders as EACH MARK IS ONE JOB — PRESS ONE FOR ITS NAME: forty-four characters of tracked uppercase mono with an em dash inside it. On this surface the label voice is a two-to-four-word stamp (OLDEST · 41 DAYS, A FORTNIGHT, THREE REFUSALS, NOT YET); no sentence is set in it anywhere. Worse, .dim resolves to --ink-3, the identical ink .strip-scale already paints its ticks in (lately.html:415), and the line would land immediately beneath that row of mono ticks — a second mono voice, shouting, in the same colour, one line under the first. It would read as another axis annotation, not as an invitation, which is the one job it was added to do. The inline margin-top:var(--gap-snug) is also a one-off outside the card's own rhythm (.ages sets its gaps at --gap-room/--gap-line). Both automated gates would stay green on this fix — data-type="label" is a legal role and #71717a on paper clears AA — which is exactly why it has to be caught by eye. (2) THE CLASS IS OVERSTATED. Nothing on this card is wrong or untrue. Every mark is placed by value, ringed to clear the 3:1 non-text floor, named in the tree, and raises its tip on pointer, keyboard and touch — interaction-check.mjs proves all three paths ("a real pointer over a mark names it", "a real touch on a mark names it", the second-tap dismiss, Escape). The seat says so itself: "the mechanism is there and works". An under-advertised affordance that works is a refinement, not a defect — and detail-on-demand with no instruction line is precisely what the named benchmarks ship: Stripe's dashboard, Vercel Analytics and Linear's insights all raise a tooltip off a mark, on touch as well as pointer, with no "press me" copy on the canvas. Grading this a defect grades the surface against a convention the benchmarks do not themselves follow. (3) THE CONSEQUENCE IS INFLATED. "WHICH three" is not "the one fact the movement was built to deliver". Movement two's stated deliverable is the counts, all five out of the same nine, plus the shape of the ages; the identity of an individual job is the Tasks destination that the round notes put on the port packet and that round 2 deliberately stopped promising. The tip is a bonus detail layer over a movement that already answers its question in the KPI row above it.
sharpenedFix:
If the panel wants the invitation anyway, do not use the stamp voice. This surface already owns a voice for a quiet explanatory line under a figure:

in sentence case, used twice in the hero ("Counted at the moment each job reached a done column." at lately.html:824, and the first-run note at :997) and once in the refusals (:908). Match it: insert after the .strip div and before the card's .sr paragraph, with no inline margin — give .ages > .t-small a margin-top of var(--gap-line) in the stylesheet so it sits on the declared ladder like everything else. Wording should state the object rather than issue a tutorial imperative, because "press" is only true under a coarse pointer (hover raises it on a fine one, focus on a keyboard): "Each mark is one open job — its name is on the mark." Keep it out of the axis's ink by using .dim (ink-3) only if it clears the ticks by position; if it reads as an annotation in situ, it is not worth the line and the honest answer is to leave the card as it is.
breaks: Adding any paragraph to .card.ages grows the card in all four states that draw a strip (full, partial, quiet, first-run) and in the loading skeleton, where .sk-wrap [data-type] turns it into a wash block — correct behaviour, but it lengthens the loading frame too. Re-measure after it lands: the ages card height at 390/768/1280/1440 in every state; that the new line does not push the strip's reserved 112px band or the axis ticks (interaction-check.mjs "no age tick leaves the strip" and "every stacked mark stays inside the strip" at each width); that a focused .dot still scrolls into view with its scroll-margin intact; the screen-reader order, since the new visible paragraph is announced immediately before the .sr line that already lists all nine titles; and the audit's type-ramp and AA contrast pass for the new data-type role on both grounds.
